seat:both-fates-from-the-start.answer_in_one_paragraph: Test 1 fails as worded, and the worked case shows less than its telling. In HigherStartEnds's world on min z (12 - z), every way has at most one level from which it never ends (from [A]: six only; five and seven both end). Below that level the level runs down with no C ever met; above it a C comes to be met and the take outruns the level. Every never-ending course sits on one of two fixed configurations (B C at 4, B B C C at 8), with ending one level either side. So no threshold, band or half-space on the start sorts the fates; the exact start conditions are equations that are the first two steps written out. In general, with a rising step map: a way's levels are cut into intervals of constant itinerary; the starts from which everyone is met for ever are an up-set; one need gives an up-set. Kids needing no more, taking the same, and a rising giving together do not.

statements.statement: HigherStartEnds, ways of up to three units, levels 0 to 12: 8 of 260 starts never end, one level per way: A 6, B 3, BB 6, BC 4, AC 7, BCC 5, BBC 7, ACC 8; the other 12 ways none. Along each way's levels: endings by running down, then that level, then endings after a C is met.

So each way's levels are cut into intervals of one itinerary and one fate, each cut a threshold of a composed level map at a need.

refute:one-space.verdict:
AI-written (Fable, refuter seat). By the three frozen tests the try has changed nothing yet. The seats' negative findings hold under an independent transcription (ways as lists, not counts). Their positive statements survive, but each is a root lemma retold or a band of one level in the worked case. The one claimed deletion of an old proof (October's lines 357-417) does not stand.
NOT YET: test 1 is met only by running the course, no proof older than 12 November is deleted, and the only shortening is about twenty lines, nearly all from a private lemma written 15 November.
survive: Root and pair forms (seat 1): true, trivially. The pair form is Lasting.avoids_iff_closed (Lasting.lean:458) said with `can`. Composed as cited it yields not-not-can, so in the axiom-free core it is closed_orbit proved again or needs Goes decided; 'six lines' is low.

Holds with level at most hi and Regime is closed under even, some, down: the paper argument checks (kids take the same, so Regime at the next way is the same). Search: 0 of 239 members left it; Holds alone was left in 13,329 steps. Small sample.

HigherStartEnds table, reproduced with lists: 1,079 starts, 17 never end, no way with two such levels; 34 starts on level = 6a+3b+c, 17 end. Added: on all 1,079, never ending equals being at a fixed going configuration within two steps.

Itinerary intervals, all-met up-set, one need (seat 2): 0 violations in 5,477 random worlds where seat 2 had not searched (use 0, need 0, childless units, levels past the ceiling). The premise doing the work is the rising step z + g z. From [A] the classes are [0], [1-4], [5], [6], [7-12]: six is an interval of one level.
Two-sided band: holds; in the worked case it is level 8 alone, which is unending_of_fixed (LineOnAStock.lean:1352).
Seat 2's countermodels reproduced: ceiling 7 under two_units_iff's premises lasts from 4 and 6, ends from 5 and 7; ceiling 6, [P,Q], lasts from 3, 5, 6, ends from 4.
Products fail: the least ways-by-levels set closed under the net and holding ([A],6) has levels 0, 2, ..., 12 and 74 members with no need met, ([A],0) among them.
Phase lemma: holds on 9,800 laws, needG = 0 and start below H included. It is three lines of algebra.

broken.claim: Seat 3: the phase lemma with the schedule comparison would delete no_return_below_support, permanently_below, overdraw_crosses_support (deeper:357-417, 57 lines).
broken.how: The three are stated and used for any needF and any schedule: permanently_below at bound needF > 0 (RelationalRenewal.lean:481); overdraw_consuming at arbitrary L in ActiveReading:89, Ranking:397, Relevance:360, HorizonWebs:110; overdraw_crosses_support in RenewalFlow:228. malignant (:518), together (:565), escalation (:590) have needF of 1 or more. The phase equation fails for needF >= 1 in 1,892 of 4,000 laws: start 1, renew 0, needG 1, needF 2, draw 1 gives Law 1,1,1 and the shifted step 1,0,0. RelationalRenewal is upstream of RegimeMargin (through Dependence), so the three would also have to move. Recount: 61 lines, 59 non-blank.
